review.tagline: Python SDK and runtime for building and serving agents behind a REST API
review.summary: Agno is a Python framework for defining agents, plus the AgentOS runtime that serves them through a REST API with 50+ endpoints, SSE and websockets. Sessions, memory, knowledge and traces are stored in your own database, and a web UI manages the running platform. It includes JWT-based RBAC, human approval steps, cron scheduling, and interfaces for Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, AG-UI and A2A.
review.audience: Python developers building self-hosted multi-user agent services
strengths: Runtime ships a REST API with 50+ endpoints, SSE and websockets
JWT-based RBAC and multi-tenant isolation included
100+ prebuilt toolkits plus OpenTelemetry tracing and audit logs
Starter templates for Docker, AWS, GCP, Azure, Fly, Render, Modal and Helm
weaknesses: Sends a telemetry event per agent run unless AGNO_TELEMETRY=false is set
README gives no RAM, GPU or port requirements
Starter templates live in separate repos, not in this one
Management UI hosting and licensing terms are not described in the README
